units.zh: 〈師古曰：「但次古人而不表今人者，其書未畢故也。」〉
units.en: 〈As Yan Shigu notes: "It lists only figures of antiquity and not contemporaries because this work was left unfinished."〉
units.literal: 〈Yan Shigu says: "The reason it only arranges ancient people and does not chart present people is that the book was not yet finished."〉

units.zh: 自書契之作，先民可得而聞者，經傳所稱，唐虞以上，帝王有號謚。
units.en: From the time writing first appeared, what the classics and commentaries preserve about the earliest ages is that rulers from the era of Yao and Shun and earlier were remembered with formal titles and posthumous names.
units.literal: Since the creation of writing, what can be heard of the former people, as named in the classics and commentaries, from the age of Yao and Shun upward, is that emperors and kings had titles and posthumous names.

units.zh: 輔佐不可得而稱矣，而諸子頗言之，雖不考虖孔氏，然猶著在篇籍，歸乎顯善昭惡，勸戒後人，故博采焉。
units.en: The chief ministers who aided those rulers cannot all be securely identified. Still, the various philosophical writings speak of them. Even when such accounts are not confirmed by the Confucian canon, they remain in the textual record and serve to highlight virtue, expose wrongdoing, and admonish later generations, so I have gathered them widely.
units.literal: Their assistants and supporters cannot be fully named. Yet the various masters discuss them somewhat; although these accounts are not verified by the Confucian tradition, they are still recorded in writings, and their purpose returns to making good manifest and evil clear, exhorting and warning later people, therefore I have collected them broadly.

units.zh: 孔子曰：「若聖與仁，則吾豈敢？」
units.en: Confucius said, "If you speak of sageliness and perfect benevolence, I would not presume to claim them."
units.literal: Confucius said: "As for being sage and benevolent, how could I dare claim that?"

units.zh: 又曰：「何事於仁，必也聖乎！」
units.en: He also said, "Why speak only of benevolence? One would have to reach sagehood."
units.literal: He also said: "How could one stop at benevolence? It would have to be sagehood!"

units.zh: 「未知，焉得仁？」
units.en: "Without understanding, how could one realize true benevolence?"
units.literal: "If one does not yet know, how can one attain benevolence?"

units.zh: 「生而知之者，上也；
units.en: "Those born with knowledge are the highest type;
units.literal: "Those who know from birth are the highest;

units.zh: 學而知之者，又其次也；
units.en: those who gain knowledge through study come next;
units.literal: those who know through learning are next;

units.zh: 困而不學，民斯為下矣。」
units.en: and those who face difficulty yet refuse to learn are the lowest among the people."
units.literal: those who are troubled yet do not learn, among the people these are the lowest."

units.zh: 又曰：「中人以上，可以語上也。」
units.en: He also said, "With people above the middle level, you can discuss higher teachings."
units.literal: He also said: "With those above the middle grade, one may speak of higher things."

units.zh: 「唯上智與下愚不移。」
units.en: "Only those of the highest wisdom and the deepest folly are unchangeable."
units.literal: "Only the highest wisdom and the lowest stupidity do not change."

units.zh: 傳曰：譬如堯舜，禹、稷、禼與之為善則行，鮌、讙兜欲與為惡則誅。
units.en: As the Tradition says: take Yao and Shun. When Yu, Ji, and Xie joined them in doing what was right, it was carried out; when Gun and Huan Dou sought to join them in wrongdoing, they were executed.
units.literal: The Tradition says: For example, with Yao and Shun, when Yu, Ji, and Xie joined them in doing good, it was carried out; when Gun and Huan Dou wished to join them in doing evil, they were executed.

units.zh: 可與為善，不可與為惡，是謂上智。
units.en: To be able to cooperate in good but never in evil—that is what is called highest wisdom.
units.literal: One can join them in doing good, but cannot join them in doing evil; this is called highest wisdom.

units.zh: 桀紂，龍逢、比干欲與之為善則誅，于莘、崇侯與之為惡則行。
units.en: By contrast, with Jie and Zhou, Long Feng and Bi Gan were executed for trying to do what was right with them, while Yuxin and the Marquis of Chong were followed when they proposed evil.
units.literal: As for Jie and Zhou, when Long Feng and Bi Gan wished to join them in doing good, they were executed; when Yuxin and the Marquis of Chong joined them in doing evil, it was carried out.

units.zh: 可與為惡，不可與為善，是謂下愚。
units.en: To be capable only of joining in evil, never in good—that is what is called utter folly.
units.literal: One can join them in doing evil, but cannot join them in doing good; this is called lowest stupidity.

units.zh: 齊桓公，管仲相之則霸，竪貂輔之則亂。
units.en: Duke Huan of Qi became hegemon when Guan Zhong served as his minister, but fell into disorder when Shu Diao assisted him.
units.literal: As for Duke Huan of Qi, when Guan Zhong served as his minister, he became hegemon; when Shu Diao assisted him, there was disorder.

units.zh: 可與為善，可與為惡，是謂中人。
units.en: Those with whom one can cooperate in either good or evil are what is called the middle type.
units.literal: One can join them in doing good and can join them in doing evil; this is called the middle type.

units.zh: 因茲以列九等之序，究極經傳，繼世相次，緫備古今之略要云。
units.en: On this basis, I set out a nine-rank order, drawing fully from the classics and commentaries, tracing each age in sequence, and assembling a concise outline of key figures from antiquity to later times.
units.literal: Accordingly I arranged the sequence of nine grades, exhausting the classics and commentaries, following generations in succession, and in sum providing the essentials of antiquity and the present.

units.zh: 〈張晏曰：「老子玄默，仲尼所師，雖不在聖，要為大賢，文伯之母達於禮典，動為聖人所歎，言為後世所則，而在第四。
units.en: 〈Zhang Yan comments: "Laozi was deep and reserved, and even Confucius learned from him. Though not classed as a sage, he was certainly a great worthy. Wenbo's mother was thoroughly versed in ritual, praised by sages for her conduct, and imitated by later generations for her words, yet she is only placed in the fourth class.
units.literal: 〈Zhang Yan says: "Laozi was profound and silent, one whom Zhongni took as teacher; though not among the sages, he was surely a great worthy. Wenbo's mother was versed in ritual canons; her conduct was praised by sages, and her words were taken as models by later ages, yet she is placed in the fourth rank.

units.zh: 田單以即墨孤城復強齊之大，魯連之博通，忽於榮利，藺子申威秦王，退讓廉頗，乃在第五。
units.en: Tian Dan revived powerful Qi from the isolated city of Jimo; Lu Zhonglian was widely learned and dismissed fame and gain; Lin Xiangru overawed the king of Qin and later yielded place to Lian Po, yet all are ranked only in the fifth class.
units.literal: Tian Dan, with the lone city of Jimo, restored mighty Qi; Lu Lian was broadly learned and indifferent to glory and profit; Master Lin demonstrated authority before the King of Qin and yielded to Lian Po, yet they are placed in the fifth rank.

units.zh: 大姬巫怪，好祭鬼神，陳人化之，國多淫祀，寺人孟子違於大雅，以保其身，旣被宮刑，怨刺而作，乃在第三。
units.en: Tai Ji indulged in shamanic superstition and spirit sacrifices, and the people of Chen followed her into proliferating illicit cults. The palace eunuch Master Meng, straying from lofty orthodox standards to save himself, later wrote resentful satires after his castration, yet is ranked in the third class.
units.literal: Great Ji was shamanistic and strange, fond of sacrificing to spirits; the people of Chen were transformed by this and the state had many excessive cults. The palace eunuch Master Meng departed from the lofty standards of the Odes to preserve his own person; after suffering castration, he wrote in resentment and satire, yet is placed in the third rank.

units.zh: 嫪毐上烝，昬亂禮度，惡不忍聞，乃在第七。
units.en: Lao Ai committed unspeakable incest and threw ritual order into chaos, crimes too vile to recount, yet he is placed in the seventh class.
units.literal: Lao Ai committed incest with one above, confounding and violating ritual norms; the evil is unbearable to hear, yet he is in the seventh rank.

units.zh: 其餘差違紛錯不少，略舉揚較，以起失謬。
units.en: There are many other inconsistencies and confusions; I mention and compare a few to highlight these mistakes.
units.literal: As for the rest, discrepancies and confusions are not few; I briefly raise and compare them to expose errors.

units.zh: 獨馳騖於數千歲之中，旁觀諸子，事業未究，而尋遇竇氏之難，使之然乎？」
units.en: He ranged alone across several millennia, examining the various schools, but before he could complete the project he was caught up in the Dou clan calamity. Is that why it ended this way?"
units.literal: Alone he galloped through several thousand years, surveying the various masters from the side; his undertaking was not finished, and then he encountered the Dou-clan disaster. Did this cause it to be so?"

units.zh: 師古曰：「六家之論，輕重不同；
units.en: Yan Shigu says: "The six traditions evaluate things differently, assigning different weights and priorities;
units.literal: Yan Shigu says: "The judgments of the six schools differ in what they treat as weighty or light;

units.zh: 百行所存，趣拾難壹。
units.en: With so many forms of conduct preserved in the record, selecting and ranking them by one standard is difficult.
units.literal: Among the hundred kinds of conduct that remain, the aims and selections are hard to unify.

units.zh: 張氏輒申所見，掎摭班史，然其所論，又自差錯。
units.en: Zhang simply advanced his own opinions and faulted Ban Gu's history, but his own arguments were themselves inconsistent.
units.literal: Master Zhang then set forth his own views and criticized Ban's history, yet what he argued also had errors of its own.

units.zh: 且年代乆遠，墳典隟亡，學者舛駮，師論分異，是以表載古人名氏，或與諸書不同。
units.en: Besides, those eras are very distant, many canonical texts were lost through gaps in transmission, scholars disagree and dispute, and learned traditions diverge. For that reason, some names in this table differ from what appears in other texts.
units.literal: Moreover, the ages are long remote, the canonical texts perished through gaps in transmission, scholars differ and refute one another, and masters' opinions are divided; therefore the names recorded in this table may in some cases differ from other books.

units.zh: 今則特有發明，用暢厥旨。
units.en: This note is offered specifically to clarify and bring out the underlying intent.
units.literal: Now there is particularly this clarification, used to make its intent clear and expansive.

units.zh: 自女媧以下，帝鴻以前，諸子傳記，互有舛駮，敘說不同，無所取正，大要知其古帝之號而已。
units.en: From Nüwa down through the age before the Yellow Emperor, the various textual traditions and biographies conflict with one another and offer no single authoritative account; at most, we can preserve the names of those ancient sovereigns.
units.literal: From Nüwa downward to before the Yellow Emperor, the various masters' records and biographies mutually contain errors and contradictions, with differing narratives and no source to take as correct; the main point is only to know the names of those ancient emperors.

units.zh: 諸人士見於史傳，彰灼可知者，無待解釋，其間幽昧者，時復及焉。」〉
units.en: For people whose deeds are clearly recorded in the historical sources, no explanation is needed; where points remain obscure, I occasionally add clarification."〉
units.literal: As for figures whose deeds are seen in histories and biographies and are manifestly knowable, they need no explanation; among them, where there is obscurity, I at times further address it."〉

findings.problem: Hanshu 022 contains a table preface and annotations by Zhang Yan and Yan Shigu. Names range from ancient allusions through later commentators, but no Chinese unit supplies a dated event or defensible personal activity endpoint for any extracted person. The existing Western dates—including annotation and commentary dates—were imported from identity knowledge rather than chapter evidence.
